senses: The presentation of realtime feedback on brainwave activity, as measured by sensors on the scalp, sometimes offered as a means of therapy.
A genre of traditional music and dance from Angola.
ety: Borrowed from Portuguese semba, from Kimbundu semba (“belly-bump”), from Proto-Bantu [Term?]. Doublet of samba.

senses: The postrevolutionary construction of a modern Mexican national identity.
A fund or foundation for the maintenance of the needy scholars in their studies.
ety: Borrowed from Middle French bourse, from Old French borse, from Latin bursa, from Ancient Greek βύρσα (búrsa). Doublet of purse, compare French bourse (“purse, fund”).

senses: Bad or wrong alignment; misalignment.
Synonym of calamondin.
To glorify or inflate the importance of a piece of news; to artificially create a sensation.
A person who experiences.
A person who has had a close encounter.
A kind of shiny padded jacket.
ety: From a British brand name, presumably from puff.

senses: someone who plays a mandolin
A cringing, fawning person.
ety: From Middle English spaynol, from Old French espaigneul (modern French épagneul), from Old Occitan espaignol, from Vulgar Latin *Hispāniolus (“Spanish”), from Hispānia (“Spain”).

senses: The view that neither the future nor the past exist (events and entities that are wholly past or wholly future do not exist at all).
The belief that only current phenomena are relevant.
The ahistorical interpretation of past phenomena in terms of current beliefs and knowledge.
Of a position which is held by a certain person permanently (in an administration or academy).
ety: From Latin numerarius, from numerus (“number”). Doublet of numéraire.

senses: Not befitting or proper for a son.
A motile asexual spore of some algae and fungi.
Given to snarling or growling.
Full of snarls.
examples: The snarly dog scared me for years until I learned it was very friendly and just lonely.

senses: Acting as a medium for sight; making use of refraction (of lenses, etc.).
A video on the social networking service X (formerly Twitter); an X video.
ety: From X (“a social networking service”) + video. Coined in July 2023 when Twitter rebranded to X; by analogy with the above sense and the pornographic website XVideos to criticise or mock the name change.

senses: male teacher (as a respectful term of address)
An oil lamp; a crusy.
ety: From Middle English crouse, from Old English crūse (“jar, cruse”), from Proto-West Germanic *krūsā, from Proto-Germanic *krūsǭ, *krūsaz (“jar, pot, collar, jug”). Cognate with German Krause (“pot with a lid”), Icelandic krús (“jar, jug”). Merged with Middle English croo (“pot, pitcher”), from Old English crōg (“crock, pitcher, vessel”). More at crock.

senses: Coryphaenoides cinereus (syn. Macrurus cinereus), a deep sea fish.
A proponent of the Haskalah.
Crazy, bonkers.
An act or process of creation.
ety: From Ancient Greek ποίησις (poíēsis), from ποιέω (poiéō, “to make”). Doublet of poesy.
examples: Metanoia is the knowledge that there can be totalities in this world totally different from what we thought. This is the sense in which metanoia is the most radical form of poiesis.

senses: A small box, usually a small cardboard box, in which matches are kept.
A little finger, the finger furthest on a hand from the thumb.
A little toe, the toe furthest on a foot from the big toe.
ety: From Dutch pinkje (literally “little finger”), which in the Holland dialects takes the form pinkie.

senses: A Dutch and Flemish alcoholic spirit, flavoured with juniper, rather like gin.
ety: Borrowed from Dutch jenever (“jenever”), from Old French genevre, from Vulgar Latin ziniperus, from Latin iūniperus (“juniper”).

senses: The act of enabling.
ety: From Middle English enhablement, equivalent to enable + -ment.

senses: A parade held in the Bahamas.
A style of goombay traditionally played on goatskin drums and cowbells during the parade.
ety: From John Canoe, the older name of the festival, perhaps named after folk hero John Canoe.
examples: Rafael sang from his stuffings, the beat swirled, the brass blasted, and in a three-month period, America bought a bargeful of the Munings' "junkanoo" sound.
Junkanoo also became established among expatriate Bahamian communities, notably in Miami and Toronto, where Junkanoo bands were to be seen at the Orange Bowl and Caribana parades respectively.

senses: An experimental heuristic method for solving a general class of computational problems by combining user procedures in the hope of obtaining a more efficient or robust procedure.
A small pancake, of Russian origin, made from buckwheat flour; traditionally served with melted butter, sour cream and caviar or smoked salmon.
ety: From Russian блины́ (bliný), plural of блин (blin, “pancake”).

senses: A short story.
A narration.
A recitative.
Someone who competes in the luge.
Having a specified kind of bladder.
Swollen like a bladder; bladdery.
Falco rusticolus, a large bird of prey that breeds on Arctic coasts and islands of North America, Europe and Asia.
ety: From Old French gerfaucon (modern French gerfaut), with the first element probably from Old High German gīr (“vulture”) (whence the German Geier).

senses: A long ditch or trench of unknown function, constructed in Neolithic Britain and Ireland.
A racecourse.
An academic curriculum.
A form of daily prayer or service.
ety: Learned borrowing from Latin cursus. Doublet of course and cour.

senses: A public house with a brewery (usually a microbrewery) attached.
The promotion of a diverse society composed of various races with different cultural backgrounds.
A landscape of an indoor setting.
The distinctive design that constitutes individual identity; a concept derived by Gerard Manley Hopkins from the ideas of the medieval philosopher Duns Scotus.
A traditional cheese from Cyprus, made from goat's and/or sheep's milk.
ety: Borrowed from Greek χαλλούμι (challoúmi), from Cypriot Arabic xallúm, from Egyptian Arabic حَلُّوم, from Sahidic Coptic ϩⲁⲗⲱⲙ (halōm, “cheese”), or ⲁⲗⲱⲙ (alōm, “cheese”), itself in turn probably a borrowing from Semitic, though in manuscripts and ostraca from 2nd century Roman Egypt, Egyptian Demotic Egyptian ḥlm is also attested with the meaning "cheese".
